name: Kermanshah
summary: Bisotun, outside Kermanshah city in the province, preserves the monumental inscription and relief commissioned by Darius I around 521 BCE. Its three cuneiform versions—Old Persian, Elamite, and Babylonian—record the political events of his accession; the site also contains remains from several earlier and later periods.

name: Sarpol-e Zahab / Serpêl
theme: The Anubanini rock relief and Lullubi history
summary: Above Sarpol-e Zahab, the Anubanini relief shows a ruler before the goddess Ishtar and defeated captives, with an Akkadian inscription identifying the Lullubi king. Scholars place it around the late Ur III or early Old Babylonian period; the exact dating is debated. The nearby reliefs make the Alvand valley an important landscape for studying the ancient western Zagros.

name: Mahabad
theme: Mahabad Republic and Kurdish political history
summary: Mahabad was the centre of the short-lived Republic of Mahabad, proclaimed in 1946. The episode is an important chapter in modern Kurdish political and cultural history.
